## Theme

<!-- parity: /theme -->

The TUI palette is data, never code. `/theme` lists every available theme
(built-ins first, then user themes) with a swatch preview; `/theme <name>`
switches immediately and persists the choice; `/theme reset` returns to
the default.

Config equivalent — the persisted theme name:

```yaml
tui:
  theme: default   # a built-in name or a user theme file stem
```

Built-in names: `default` (the historical site palette — teal `#5eead4`,
indigo `#818cf8`), `catppuccin`, `nord`, `dracula`, `ohmypi-dark`,
`ohmypi-light`, `pi`.

User themes live in `~/.fah/themes/<name>.json`; the file stem is the
theme name, and a user theme can never shadow a built-in (a clashing file
name is skipped with a boot note). The JSON holds a `"roles"` object mapping ROLE names to hex colors
(`"#rgb"` or `"#rrggbb"`): `accent`, `accent2`, `muted`, `highlight`,
`success`, `warning`, `error`, `border`, `focusBorder`, `userMessageBg`.
Every role is optional — a missing role inherits the default theme for
that slot. Unknown role names, invalid hex, or broken JSON produce a
named error (file, role, line) at load time, never a crash.

Applies: `/theme <name>` switches the live session in one frame; a direct
YAML edit takes effect at next boot. Asked to create a theme from a
description, write the JSON file, then apply it with `/theme <name>` and
confirm the swatch line with the user. Asked for a palette "like X" where
X is unknown, ask two or three palette questions first — never invent one
silently.

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Console-output behavior flags (gh-1198 + gh-1433), user file. Today one

run (the reasoning liveness line returns), and `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy`

hosts that parse the log. Rendered deltas — thinking AND streamed text,
on every face — pass through the redaction pipeline at render time since
gh-1433: a registered secret echoed in a delta is masked live, so
byte-pin tests for interactive `--stream-thinking` sessions must assume
redacted deltas whenever redaction is enabled (default).

```yaml

  streamThinking: false # interactive line mode only; headless runs stream by default
```

## Tool-result & user-message spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and
the session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678).
An oversized USER message (headless prompt, TUI input, steering) spills
to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/user-<n>.md` and the model receives a
bounded head+tail preview plus a read-in-parts instruction (issue
#1760). Tolerant parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as
`[spills]` notes at boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills — it beats the `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` /
`FAH_USER_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knobs too); `threshold: 0` disables
tool-result spilling only, `userThreshold: 0` the user path only:

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills; 0 = tools off
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
  userThreshold: 16384 # absolute byte floor for the user path; 0 = user off
  userFraction: 0.5 # spill a user message over this fraction of the live window budget
```

Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Project context budget

<!-- parity: notices on both surfaces; the byte knob is a config-file setting -->

`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md`/`GOAL.md`/`DESIGN.md` + Copilot

```yaml

```

## Auto update

<!-- parity: /update, settings hub -->

User file top-level key (issue #1377). The self-update policy — a
tri-state, because the honest default is neither silent-off nor
unattended-on:

```yaml
auto_update: true # true | false | "notify" (default notify)
```

`notify` (the default) checks the release feed once at boot and prints
when a newer version exists — nothing is downloaded. `true` is the
unattended arm: at boot a newer release is downloaded, provenance
verified and installed, and the session restarts onto the new binary.
`false` touches no update host at all. An absent key and an explicit
`"notify"` are the same policy — the default is never written. Strict
parse: anything but `true`, `false` or `"notify"` is a
`ConfigException`. Applies at next boot. `/update` runs a check-and-apply
immediately regardless of the policy; the settings hub exposes the same
tri-state.

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: sidecars land in `.fah/spills/sessionless/` — the AC8 "existing retention rules" claim is false, artifacts accumulate forever**

The PR description (AC8) states documents land "at `.fah/spills/<sid>/transcript-<n>.json` **with the store's existing retention rules**" and E15 promises "bounded artifacts". In practice every sidecar write goes to the `sessionless` bucket:

- `transcribeAudioTool` wires `SpillStore(sessionId: () => null, ...)` — a hardcoded null, unlike the spill hooks, which pass `() => _session?.cachedId` and therefore resolve to the real session id once the session exists (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_spill.dart:45`, `:104`).
- `SpillStore.write` then computes `.fah/spills/${sid ?? 'sessionless'}/...` (`lib/src/spill/spill.dart:454`).
- Session retention — the only workspace-spill cleanup — deletes `.fah/spills/<sessionId>` strictly per known session: `await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}')` (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:1180`; the boot sweep walks the same per-session path at `:715`). No code path ever touches `.fah/spills/sessionless/`.

So in any project using `output: sidecar` (or `auto` past the byte budget), every transcription permanently adds a file to `<cwd>/.fah/spills/sessionless/` that is never freed — unbounded workspace growth, and the advertised retention story does not hold. (The tests even pin the `sessionless` path at `test/tools/transcribe_audio_timestamps_test.dart:451`, so this is the shipped behavior, not an accident of my reading.)

Suggested directions:
- Give the plugin a session-id seam — e.g. add a lazy `sessionId` provider to `PluginContext` (populated from the same `_session?.cachedId` source the spill wiring uses), or
- route transcript sidecars through the existing tool-result spill hook chain instead of a private store, or
- at minimum, correct the AC8/E15 claims and add an explicit cleanup story for `sessionless` transcript files.

Note `PluginContext` (`lib/src/plugins/plugin.dart:45`) currently has no session-id field at all, so this needs a small plugin-API change — but shipping the retention claim as-is would document a guarantee the code cannot keep.

💡 **SUGGESTION: error-body truncation can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair**

```dart
final head = body.trim().length > 2000
    ? '${body.trim().substring(0, 2000)}…[truncated]'
    : body.trim();
```

`String.substring` cuts on UTF-16 code units. If code unit 2000 is a high surrogate (e.g. the body contains non-BMP characters — exactly the Cyrillic/emoji-bearing provider error bodies this endpoint family returns), the result carries an unpaired surrogate, which can surface as a replacement character (or an encoding exception if the message is later JSON-encoded into a tool result). Purely cosmetic in an error path, but the sibling spill code already handles this correctly (`lib/src/spill/spill.dart` `_safeCut`-style surrogate adjustment before substring). Worth reusing the same guard here.

Review complete. Verdict: **REQUEST_CHANGES** — 2 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 2 SUGGESTION.

## Summary

I reviewed PR #1890 (timestamped transcription, +2615/−29 across 8 files) against the ticket, the full source of every changed file, and the repo's spill/retention internals. I also ran the PR's claimed gates: `dart analyze` is clean on all touched files and `dart test test/tools/ test/plugins/` passes **864/864** — every gate claim in the description holds. The test coverage is genuinely thorough (request formation, degradation ladder, secret hygiene, injection-as-data, 25MB boundary).

**Two real correctness gaps remain (both BLOCKING, both verified against the checked-out code):**

1. **`require: word` silently degrades on a 200-without-words response** (`transcribe_audio.dart:545-547`). The hard-error path for `require: word` exists only on the 400 branch. If an endpoint silently ignores `timestamp_granularities[]` and returns `verbose_json` with segments but no words, the tool returns a *successful document* with just a warning — violating AC5/Q4's "hard failure below the demanded level". I proved this with a probe test (result: `warnings=[word-timings-unsupported], words=null`); the existing IT-03 test only exercises the 400 path. Same pattern for `require: segment` with a segment-less payload (no warning at all).

2. **Sidecar retention claim is false** (`transcribe_audio.dart:624-626`). The SpillStore is wired with a hardcoded `sessionId: () => null` (unlike the spill hooks, which resolve `_session?.cachedId`), so every transcript sidecar lands in `.fah/spills/sessionless/` — and the only workspace-spill cleanup (`session_retention.dart:1180`) deletes `.fah/spills/<sessionId>` per known session. Nothing ever removes `sessionless`, contradicting AC8's "existing retention rules" and E15's "bounded artifacts" and causing unbounded workspace growth. Fixing it needs a small plugin-API seam (`PluginContext` has no session id today).

Plus: `maxInlineBytes` uses a raw `as int` cast that bypasses the file's own actionable-error style (IMPORTANT), a surrogate-pair-splitting truncation in `_throwHttpError` that `_headExcerpt` already solves (SUGGESTION), and five copy-pasted enum parsers that collapse into one generic helper (SUGGESTION).

Artifacts written: `outputs/pr_review.json`, `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1..5*.md`. All inline anchors are added lines in the diff; the probe test file was removed and the tree is clean.
